BARCELONA, Nov 22 : Barcelona shook off a sloppy first half to beat Villarreal 3-2 in LaLiga on Sunday. Villarreal raced into a two-goal lead after seven minutes, as Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi took advantage of lax Barcelona play early on. Lamine Yamal won a penalty midway through the first half, but dragged the spot-kick onto the post in the 23rd minute. Gerard Martin headed in a Pedri cross in the 57th minute to reduce the gap, before Fermin Lopez equalised four minutes later.

Barcelona remain top of the standings on 36 points, three ahead of Real Madrid after Jose Mourinho's side beat Celta Vigo on Saturday. Villarreal remain ninth on 15 points.

LAS VEGAS, Nov 22 : Formula One stewards handed Mexican Sergio Perez a five-place grid penalty for next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix after ruling the Cadillac driver caused a collision with Haas' Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara in Las Vegas on Saturday. • Perez would have collected a 10 second penalty but because he had retired from the race it was changed to a grid drop for his next race instead • The stewards said Perez had not earned the right to the corner and was wholly to blame for the lap 18 collision on approaching turn 14 • "I was alongside him and expected him to leave me enough room to make the corner," said Perez. "I was planning to make the move afterwards, into Turn 16, but unfortunately he didn’t see me. By the time I tried to avoid him, it was already too late. He apologised afterwards and explained that he simply hadn’t seen me."

COP31 climate talks collapse as EU and others reject deal

The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted by all parties was in Copenhagen in 2009.

ANTALYA: United Nations climate talks collapsed on Sunday (Nov 22) as the European Union and others rejected a final draft deal put forward by COP31 presidents Türkiye and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming. The failed talks reflect world governments' struggle this year to muster ambitious action to address the worsening consequences of climate change, as wars, economic pressures and other crises compete for their attention. After more than two weeks of negotiations that spilt two days into overtime - making it the longest COP on record - Türkiye's conference president Murat Kurum said at the closing plenary that he could see there was no agreement and confirmed he would not advance any new text. "There is nothing to do, we did all that we could," he said. "There will be no new text from now on."

He later left the stage in the midst of speeches being delivered by country representatives. Australia's COP31 President of Negotiations, Chris Bowen, called the outcome "very disappointing" and said disagreements over fuels and climate finance were the dealbreakers. The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted by all parties was in Copenhagen in 2009. Ireland's environment minister Darragh O'Brien said the European Union could not support the proposed deal in part because it made no mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say drive global warming. "It is unconscionable that we would have a climate act that makes no reference to fossil fuel, no reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels," he said. Saudi Arabia and other big oil producer countries had lobbied hard to keep their mention out of the text, according to observers at the summit. Panama also said it could not support the text because it failed to address the scale and urgency of the climate crisis. This year's COP is the first since the UN's environmental body in October confirmed the rise in global temperature was set to exceed 1.5°C, a threshold countries agreed at Paris climate talks over a decade ago to try not to exceed, and beyond which extreme weather impacts intensify.

Related:

Fossil fuels still missing from latest COP31 draft deal

OPEC speaks up for fossil fuels at COP31 climate talks

Belgium's Climate Minister Jean-Luc Crucke said the failure of the deal was a difficult outcome, but appropriate. "It's not the end of multilateralism, but there has to be courage to say no," he said. While a blow to efforts to ratchet up international action, the failure to agree on a political declaration in Antalya does not erase the obligations agreed by previous UN conferences or remove the technical and legal frameworks governing multilateral action against climate change. PRESSURE FROM SAUDI ARABIA AND OTHER OIL PRODUCERS The failed deal had acknowledged the planet's projected temperature overshoot and called for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse it. That was a big ask from oil - producing countries. While scientists say removing carbon from the atmosphere - when paired with steep emissions cuts - is vital to avoiding the worst impacts of climate change, critics of the proposed deal said they worried the carbon removal language would be used as a licence to keep pumping oil. A representative for the Saudi delegation, which supported the deal's mention of carbon removal, told the summit at the closing plenary that he was surprised at the resistance to technology, which he said offered a concrete solution. Developing countries had also criticised the deal for not providing sufficient new climate finance to help them adapt to a warming planet. The deal had called for a tripling of such finance, but did not specify from what baseline. The failed deal had also included a goal put forward by Türkiye to expand electricity's share of total final world energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035, from around 23 per cent now. Proponents of that pledge said it could cut greenhouse gas emissions by speeding the transition away from fuel-powered cars, furnaces, and other equipment. But critics said it could force more costs onto poor nations without providing a clear path away from fossil fuels. The COP process is the main vehicle through which countries coordinate their efforts to curb global warming. Its annual meeting provides an opportunity for nations to signal they are willing to work together to find solutions and help finance the problems rising temperatures cause.

Source: Reuters/dc

MANCHESTER, England,, Nov 22 : Manchester City missed out on the chance to move into first place in the Women's Super League on Sunday, suffering a 3-1 defeat at home by Tottenham Hotspur that leaves them second in the standings.  With leaders Chelsea held to a 1-1 draw by Liverpool on Saturday, reigning champions City looked set to capitalise on that slip-up when they took a 1-0 lead thanks to a Bunny Shaw goal in the 10th minute. However, Norwegian striker Cathinka Tandberg levelled for Spurs just before the break.  City stuttered in attack, and they were punished in the 74th minute when Drew Spence sliced them open with a pass through the middle that Matilda Vinberg picked up before slotting into the net, and Jessica Naz added a goal on her 100th WSL appearance shortly afterwards to make it 3-1.  The defeat leaves City on 25 points after 11 games, two behind Chelsea and two ahead of third-placed London City Lionesses, while the win lifts Spurs to fifth on 20 points.  In the day's other early kick-off, Simi Awujo struck deep into second-half stoppage time to give Manchester United a 2-1 win away to Birmingham City to leave them fourth in the table on 21 points.

Source: Reuters

GURGL, Austria, Nov 22 : Timon Haugan held off compatriot Eirik Hystad Solberg to win the men's World Cup slalom in Gurgl as Norway claimed the top two places on Sunday. Haugan clocked a combined time of one minute 42.55 seconds to finish 0.60 seconds ahead of Solberg, with Switzerland's Tanguy Nef completing the podium, 0.88 behind. "It's a huge relief," Haugan told Viaplay after claiming his seventh World Cup victory and becoming the first Norwegian to win a World Cup race at the Austrian venue. Gurgl joined the World Cup calendar in 2023. Haugan had endured a difficult build-up to the season after discovering he had used the wrong binding setup for much of his preparation.

"It's been one of the toughest pre-seasons I've had, with a lot of doubt and uncertainty. I thought I just had to go for it today. Better to do it now than later," he added. Solberg delivered a strong second run to secure the first World Cup podium of his career. "It doesn't get any more fun than that," Solberg said. Atle Lie McGrath, who trailed Haugan by just one hundredth of a second after the opening run, failed to finish his second descent. Fellow Norwegian Henrik Kristoffersen also went out in the deciding run. Brazil's Lucas Pinheiro Braathen saw his bid to win the opening three races of the season end when he straddled a gate early in the first run. He had won the giant slalom in Soelden and the slalom in Levi.

PORTIMAO, Nov 22 : Ducati's Marc Marquez sealed the 2026 MotoGP crown at the Portuguese Grand Prix on Sunday, his eighth-place finish enough to establish an unassailable lead in the standings and place him alongside the great Giacomo Agostini on eight premier-class titles. Marquez needed to finish in the top nine in Sunday's race and despite starting second on the grid, the Spaniard rode with caution to finish eighth and seal the title with a round to spare. The race was won by Marco Bezzecchi, who held a 102-point advantage over Marquez at one stage this season, while his Aprilia team mate Jorge Martin and Trackhouse rider Raul Fernandez completed the podium. However, all eyes were on Marquez, who marked the occasion by scaling a scaffold to address the cheering fans before watching a big-screen montage of the defining moments of his career.

MARQUEZ, THE 'GOAT' As a final flourish, the Spaniard ascended a staircase accompanied by the silhouette of a goat on the screen, a nod to his growing 'Greatest of All Time' status, before receiving a golden commemorative helmet from Agostini himself. He then attached another plaque with his name engraved on it on the Tower of Champions before embracing and lifting it over his head. "We need to be happy. I know that we are here celebrating a historic moment. I know how I suffered," said an emotional Marquez, who underwent double surgery midway through the season. "I know that in the middle of the season, the fans believed more than I did. My people believed more than I did. But I kept pushing, I kept doing my best. "I said last year that it was a championship where I was at peace with myself. This one is for all the fans that believed in me from 2020 until now. So thanks to all of you, this is for all of you." Marquez came agonisingly close to securing the title in Saturday's sprint but his hopes were dashed when he crashed out on the penultimate lap while running in third place, a finish that would have been sufficient to crown him champion. But unlike Saturday's overcast conditions and spots of rain on the circuit, Sunday's 25-lap race was held in bright sunshine. TOP-NINE FINISH ENOUGH FOR MARQUEZ Martin needed to outscore Marquez by 18 points while the Ducati rider's equation was far more simple: secure a top-nine finish regardless of his rivals' results to get his hands on the trophy. Marquez had been cautious in the sprint but this time he shot off the line to take the lead from polesitter Bezzecchi while several riders jostled for position behind him, with Martin moving up from seventh to fourth. But Marquez was soon swallowed up by the faster Aprilia bikes around him, with the championship leader quickly falling to seventh as he exercised caution amid aggressive overtaking. A crash from Pedro Acosta moved Marquez up to sixth but he had to concede two places to Fabio Di Giannantonio and Ai Ogura, with the Ducati rider happy to open the door to let them pass knowing eighth would be good enough for the title. Up front, Bezzecchi finally moved past Fernandez to take the lead on lap 15 while Martin also found a way past three laps later with an identical overtake to make it a factory Aprilia one-two. On lap 19, Marquez fell to ninth as KTM's Brad Binder nudged him aside to overtake and there was concern from his legion of fans at the Algarve International Circuit, but a crash from Diogo Moreira on the last lap moved Marquez up to eighth. "Super happy about the season, obviously some highs and some lows, but my best season in MotoGP so far," said Bezzecchi, who missed races with his own injuries. "Still a lot of things to improve. But congrats to Marc, he really deserves everything. He's one of the strongest riders in history, so to fight with him is an honour. "Hopefully next year I will fight again and make his life even harder."

Nov 22 : Paris St Germain forward Desire Doue will undergo surgery later this month after suffering a serious right knee injury, the Ligue 1 champions said on Sunday, with no timeline yet set for his return. The 21-year-old France international was carried off in tears towards the end of the first half of PSG's 3-2 victory at Nice on Saturday after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee. Doue had earlier scored his second league goal of the season, but was injured when his fully extended leg buckled as he turned to shield the ball from Nice midfielder Sofiane Diop, with no contact between the players. The injury is the latest setback for Doue, who missed parts of last season with calf and hamstring problems.

Nov 22 : South Africa have made two changes to their starting XI for the second and final test against Bangladesh in Centurion on Monday, with batter Tony de Zorzi and fast bowler Anrich Nortje included as the home side seek to win the series. Stand-in captain Aiden Markram confirmed the team on Sunday with De Zorzi included in place of regular skipper Temba Bavuma, who has a calf injury. Nortje comes into the side for Dane Paterson. South Africa won the first test by nine wickets, strengthening their position at the top of the World Test Championship table as they look to defend the title they claimed against Australia at Lord’s last year.   Markram said the wicket looks as though it will have pace and bounce as the game goes on.

"This looks like a pretty typical Centurion wicket," he said. "Generally, it can start off on the slower side and it just quickens up throughout the game. "It's known for a bit of pace and bounce, but also known as a venue where you can score big runs if you get in." Markram has stood in for Bavuma before and said the way the team operates will make it easy for him to do so again. "We've worked really well, to be honest," he said. "Temba is still going to be around this week, so I think it's quite a smooth transition, if there even is a transition. "Shuks (coach Shukri Conrad) is obviously really strong in his ways as well, and from my point of view, it's just about trying to carry those good things forward and trying to get a pulse of the game as quickly as you can, assessing conditions as quickly as you can and coming up with plans from there." Bangladesh scored 400 in their first innings at The Wanderers and took the test to the fifth day. Markram praised their application and expects more of the same at Centurion. "They batted well. They made 400 in the first innings, and first-innings runs, especially of that amount, will keep you in the game for quite a long period of time," he said.

NEW YORK, Nov 22 : For the second time this year, Wall Street bankers and lawyers took home a massive paycheck from a record-setting initial public offering. And for the second time this year, some of them came out of it complaining in private about how the process was riddled with complications and unlike any they had worked on before. With SpaceX’s IPO in June, in which banks earned half a billion dollars in fees, bankers chafed over how tightly the Elon Musk-led company controlled the months-long process and kept financial and other information private, making it hard for advisers to do their jobs.  As Anthropic’s IPO, dubbed internally “Project Lantern”, eclipsed SpaceX on Thursday and bankers took home more than half a billion dollars in fees, several people close to the process listed a litany of problems that had plagued the offering process: a compressed timeline, marred by last-minute changes and delays in sharing financial projections; rushed document approvals; and highly unusual restrictions on bankers and concern about leaks — especially after Reuters reported many details from a draft IPO filing weeks before it was made public. Anthropic, for example, instructed some of its 22 IPO underwriters to limit the number of bankers working on the deal to four, asking the firms to make sure they were senior staff, several people familiar with the matter said. One of the people said the restriction likely came out of fear that information would leak, and that the banks found a way to work around it anyway.

Underlying these complaints is a new power dynamic between technology companies and Wall Street. Companies such as SpaceX, Anthropic — and potentially also OpenAI in the future —  have come to wield enormous power as the transformative potential of artificial intelligence creates a frenzied demand for their shares, and they are wielding it to do things their way. That is upsetting some bankers. But banks and investors appear to have little choice but to play along. “These companies certainly did have some market power to tell underwriters that it’s not going to be business as usual,” said Jay Ritter, a University of Florida professor emeritus who researches IPOs. “But the big Wall Street firms, I suspect, are still going to be doing things as business as usual for all but maybe OpenAI (after these two deals).” Ritter added that both SpaceX and Anthropic had negotiated to pay underwriters nothing on the additional shares sold through the greenshoe option. “I don't think most companies are going to be able to demand zero spread on overallotment shares,” he said. Anthropic, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, the two lead underwriters on the two IPOs, declined to comment. SpaceX and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment. Both SpaceX and Anthropic debuted successfully, raising record amounts of money, and their shares rallied initially. A key part of the underwriters’ job is to market the securities. Thanks to the demand for AI, that was an easy sell — both companies had order books oversubscribed many times over.  After an initial burst in shares, the trajectories of the two big AI firms diverged. SpaceX climbed to a post-listing peak of $201.80 on June 16 before retreating below its $135 IPO price for the first time in mid-July. Anthropic’s shares closed down 8.5 per cent on Friday after a 17 per cent first-day pop, as a dramatic unraveling of the AI trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector. UNUSUAL NON-COMPETES AND RESTRICTIONS In the case of SpaceX’s IPO, the people close to the process said Musk’s team dictated terms at every stage. Musk's team told the largest and most powerful US banks — including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley — how to market SpaceX's stock and to whom. It told some banks the specific order sizes they needed to “fill” — in some cases a few billion dollars — and gave them instructions on what types of investors to bring. Banks signed on to underwrite the IPO without being told what they would be paid, the people said. The underlying current running through Anthropic’s IPO process was what several of the people who spoke to Reuters interpreted as a sense of extreme caution.     Anthropic asked some senior officers at banks working on its IPO to sign legal documents restricting core members of the transaction team from working with rival companies, including OpenAI, Cursor, DeepSeek and Hugging Face, for six months after it went public, according to the people.  Banks routinely manage conflicts and protect client confidentiality. But bankers and lawyers said it is rare for an IPO to impose exclusivity this broad, particularly on individual bankers.  In previous head-to-head IPOs such as those of ridesharing rivals Uber and Lyft, or real estate companies Trulia and Zillow, banks could simply pick a side, in part because the deals were smaller and required fewer banks.  Anthropic, by contrast, needed a broad syndicate to raise the enormous amount of capital it was seeking. That, some of the people said, explained why Anthropic sought to bind individual bankers with these restrictions.  One banker who declined to sign on to the agreement said it was a challenge to find people who could promise not to actively cover or engage with Anthropic’s peers, especially as several of those companies pursue their own initial or secondary offerings.   INFORMATION LEAKS AND LATE NIGHTS  Some of the restrictions were meant to control leaks of information.  Nearly four weeks before Anthropic’s filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, called Form S-1, was made public, Reuters reported on it, revealing details of the company’s financials, risk factors, dealings with other tech companies and other information.  Anthropic also used a product called NetRoadshow to share information, instead of regular PDFs, with most of the banks underwriting the deal.  NetRoadshow logs access details, including information such as who has seen the document and looked at which page. Documents on NetRoadshow also had individual bankers’ names as watermarks.  Leaks continued to surface in the press, but using NetRoadshow complicated bankers' work, including because the platform would not let them save copies of documents, one of the people said. Anthropic planned to file an updated securities filing, called an S-1A, with the SEC with the price range and to launch the marketing on November 10. To do so, it needed to send a draft to all the banks in its syndicate for them to sign off on it. The night before it was to happen, a law firm on the deal sent a PDF to the banks about the sale of shares in Canada. But soon it followed with another email asking them to disregard it, saying it “contains incorrect price range and share information,” according to the email, which was seen by Reuters.   The correct S-1A was then sent via the NetRoadshow platform around 2 a.m. New York time. Banks were told they had several hours to sign off on it before it was filed with the SEC.

Source: Reuters

Nov 22 : Captain Bruno Fernandes said Manchester United have offered him a new contract but discussions have been put on hold as the club focuses on turning around its poor form. Fernandes' current deal expires at the end of the season, although United hold an option to extend the midfielder's contract by a further year until June 2028, giving the club more time to reach an agreement on fresh terms. "Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on," Fernandes told Sky Sports in an interview published on Sunday. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but because of the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

LAS VEGAS, Nov 22 : Ferrari principal Fred Vasseur said Charles Leclerc's collision with teammate Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday was "completely unacceptable". The incident came weeks after the Ferrari pair had collided at the Mexico City race, prompting talks within the team aimed at preventing a repeat. Vasseur said the latest clash was particularly frustrating given Ferrari had addressed the issue with both drivers after Mexico and again in Brazil. Leclerc received a 10-second penalty over the incident and finished 10th, while Hamilton, who was penalised for an earlier incident, finished seventh.

"Clearly it's unacceptable, first," Vasseur told Sky Italia. "A bit the same message as Mexico because you have to think about the team, about the people working in Maranello, about all the stakeholders, sponsors." Leclerc had attempted to pass his teammate on the inside during the latter stages of the race but the pair made contact that spun Hamilton around. "Charles did clearly make a mistake, that is penalising the team a lot and it's completely unacceptable today," Vasseur said. "We had a chat all together in Brazil. Today we passed the message to think about the team when they were racing together and the outcome is this one. It's mega-frustrating for all of us." Leclerc said he accepted responsibility as the stewards had decided to penalise him. "I've been penalised so as a result I guess the majority and the stewards thought that it was my mistake, which I'll accept," the Monegasque driver added. "I'm not going to say much more. At the end of the day I'm penalised so it has to be my mistake. "I just feel quite embarrassed for the team in general. We will review." Hamilton was reluctant to discuss the clash with Leclerc. "I'm not going to get into the scenario. That's something for you to speak to Ferrari about," Hamilton said. "But we knew that we were faced with a massive challenge this weekend. We didn't realise there would be such a limitation on the straights, and qualifying obviously was difficult. "In the race I felt great and I really was progressing well. We ultimately wanted to try and make sure we finished ahead of the McLarens because that's who we're really fighting in the constructors." Hamilton was penalised on lap 12 for leaving the track and gaining an advantage while passing McLaren's Lando Norris. The seven-times world champion was unable to give the position back and said the sanction was harsh. "Avoiding collision with one of the McLarens got me a 10-second penalty, which was, I think, really harsh," he said. "I got my head back down and just kept chasing, managed to get back in the fight and then got knocked back again. "But I never gave up and was just trying to get the best result. I really think we could have had a podium today with the pace we had." Asked whether Ferrari needed firmer internal rules for racing Hamilton said that was a matter for the team. "That's for Ferrari to decide, honestly," he said. "I've done all I can and I've said everything and more. It's been difficult. So all I can do is just show up and give it everything I can and hope in the background they eventually figure it out."

Source: Reuters

LAS VEGAS, Nov 21 : McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri said they were pleased to put last year's double disqualification at the Las Vegas Grand Prix behind them after finishing second and third on Saturday. Norris had started from pole position and finished second in Las Vegas last year, while Piastri crossed the line fourth, but both were later disqualified for excessive skid plank wear. On Saturday, Norris and Piastri followed home race winner Max Verstappen, with Piastri joking that he would save his celebrations until the final technical checks were complete. "I don't know if we're past scrutineering yet. I'm hoping we have," the Australian told reporters. "No, it's good. And yeah, in the context of this year's championship it's exactly what we needed.

"He speaks a lot next to the track," Verstappen told the post-race press conference of Russell. "It doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me to try and challenge that. "And today karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. "So I was like 'fantastic. My day's only getting better'." Canada's 1997 world champion Jacques Villeneuve, a pundit for Sky Sports television, winced at the comments. "The comments are there to hurt, to put in his terms George in place," he said. "From the outside you just have to laugh and find the fun in the words that are being used." Russell said he had no regrets about the move that left him in the barriers. "I felt like I had to go for it if I wanted to win the race," he added. "In a race like this it was sort of high risk, high reward and with two laps remaining I kind of really wanted to be behind Max going into that last lap and obviously just got it very slightly wrong, and with the lockup it was unavoidable. "So obviously disappointed and a bit frustrated with it." (Writing by Alan Baldwin in London; Editing by Peter Rutherford)

The governor of Washington state denounced federal immigration authorities on Saturday (Nov 21) for arresting two people on a jetway at a Seattle-area airport. The incident involving Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers occurred around 8am PST at the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport as people boarded an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles. ICE officers conducted an operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, who overstayed his visa, the agency said in a statement. The officers also arrested a second individual, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, who threw hot coffee at them, ICE said in a post on social media. Mejia had also overstayed her visa, ICE said, adding that she would be charged with assaulting a federal officer. Reuters was not able to identify lawyers for Mendoza or Mejia.

"ICE is completely and totally out of control and today we are confronted with yet more evidence of this," said Governor Bob Ferguson, a Democrat, at a news conference on Saturday. Video of the incident circulated on social media and news outlets is "horrific" and "chilling", Ferguson said, adding that he told Alaska Airlines representatives that “they need to call on ICE to get out of our airports." The governor said he would make the same request of every other airline that flies out of Sea-Tac airport. Alaska Airlines said it is "concerned" by the federal action. "Alaska Airlines was not provided advance notice of the enforcement action and we are working to understand the circumstances surrounding what occurred," the company said in a statement. April Sims, president of the Washington State Labor Council called the ICE arrest a "smash-and-grab" action that injected fear and chaos during a delicate time for air travel. "Just days after our nation experienced widespread disruptions to air travel and flights being grounded, federal agents chose to carry out this operation at one of our busiest airports, during one the busiest travel weeks of the year," Sims said in a statement sent by the union, which includes local chapters representing flight attendants and ground crew at Sea-Tac airport. Alaska Airlines said many passengers were put on other flights shortly after the incident and the originally scheduled flight departed at 11am.

Source: Reuters/nh
